title: City payments plus audited federal money from elsewhere, against the revenue on the return
question: Adding what the City paid to the federal money the organization’s own audit says came from elsewhere, does the total fit inside the revenue it reported to the tax authority?
finding: In nearly every case it does. Of 542 return-years with both an audit and City payments, 11 at 9 organizations show the two together above total revenue by $250,000 and 5% or more: Main Street Launch (year ended 2021-06-30: $4.1 million City plus $76.4 million other federal, against $12.8 million revenue); Children's Council of San Francisco (year ended 2023-06-30: $166.5 million City plus $21.0 million other federal, against $174.8 million revenue); The SF Housing Accelerator Fund (year ended 2025-06-30: $44.7 million City plus $5.0 million other federal, against $42.5 million revenue); Conard House Inc (year ended 2025-06-30: $18.5 million City plus $3.5 million other federal, against $19.8 million revenue).
how: For each return with a single audit for the same employer number and year end: City payments (the payment table, spread onto the tax year) plus the audit’s federal spending that did not come through the City (loans left out), against total revenue on the return. The reconcile screens already test City money alone; this adds the second payer.
limits: An audit records federal money spent, a return records revenue earned, and the City ledger records cash paid, so a year can differ by timing alone. Money an organization passes straight on (child-care subsidies, loan capital, rent paid for clients) may be booked as an agency transaction and never as revenue. A lender’s audit counts loan guarantees. Each row is a reason to read the audited statements beside the return. For the fiscal years covered here, the federal audit threshold depends on the start of the entity’s fiscal year. It was $750,000 in federal awards expended across all programs for years starting before October 1, 2024, and $1 million for years starting on or after that date. An entity reaches the threshold at either amount. City payments alone cannot establish how much federal funding the recipient expended.
